current is also expected for east and southeast-facing beaches.

* WHEN...Today.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...South winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 80 mph. Wind gusts

near Brian Head as of 755 AM.

* WHERE...Southern Mountains.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM MDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles and vehicles with trailers.

or damaged by the wind.

properties.description:

extending from near Asheboro to 11 miles north of Rockingham, moving
east at 30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Asheboro, Randleman, Troy, North Carolina Zoo, Biscoe, Seagrove,
Ramseur, Mount Gilead, Franklinville, and Robbins.

This includes Interstate 73 between Mile Markers 28 and 81.
properties.instruction:
A Tornado Watch remains in effect until 500 PM EDT for central North
Carolina.

Remain alert for a possible tornado! Tornadoes can develop quickly
from severe thunderstorms. If you spot a tornado go at once into the
basement or small central room in a sturdy structure.

Straight line winds can blow down trees, power lines, and damage
mobile homes and other buildings. Seek shelter in a sturdy structure
until the storm has passed. Stay away from windows as flying debris
generated by damaging winds can be deadly.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Portions of western North Carolina, including the following

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

rainfall will keep high water levels in portions of the area.

- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
A Flood Watch for flash flooding means there is a potential for rapid
onset flooding based on current forecasts. Flash flooding is a very
dangerous situation and may impact areas that do not typically flood.
Please monitor the latest forecasts and be prepared to take action
quickly should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

Rainfall of more than five inches in similar storms has been
associated with an increased risk of landslides, especially
fast-moving debris flows and debris slides. If you live on a
mountainside or in a cove at the base of a mountain, especially near
a stream, be ready to leave in advance of the storm and follow
evacuation orders from local officials. Consider postponing travel
along mountain roads during the heavy rainfall event.
